apps.name: SEUsign
apps.localizedDescription: SEUsign is a free on-device iOS application manager and signer. Sign, install and manage your own apps straight from your device.
apps.subtitle: On-device signing application

news.title: SEUsign 4.3.1
news.caption: The app now adds the SEU community repository (DatOneFlareon/The-SEU-app-repo-for-the-gangalang) as a source on first launch, so its apps arrive in Sources without pasting the URL by hand. It is added once: deleting it later is respected, and a failed fetch is retried next launch.

news.title: SEUsign 4.2.0
news.caption: Certificates from sideloading.net are now all selectable. The list opens on All, every row imports in one tap, and a revoked or expired certificate asks for confirmation first instead of being impossible to pick. Density and card shape now reshape the real lists: Library, Sources and source app rows draw on a shared card surface with row insets, icon sizes, spacing and corner radius driven by those settings, and the Appearance preview is the same real row.

news.title: SEUsign 4.1.0
news.caption: Certificate uploads now ask first: remote verification and password recovery show a plain warning that the .p12 and its password go to sideloading.net before anything leaves your device. Density and card shape now change the Library and Sources lists, and a new Unable to Verify App screen explains Apple's developer trust check, tests ocsp.apple.com and ppq.apple.com, and opens VPN & Device Management. Certificates are also re-checked for revocation on every launch, so a revoked certificate is flagged before it signs anything.

news.title: SEUsign 4.0.0
news.caption: Automatic certificates from sideloading.net: browse the published list, let the app pick the certificate with the longest validity, import it in one tap, verify a certificate remotely, or recover a .p12 password with the wordlist service. Plus new interface styles, density, card shape and background options.

news.title: SEUsign 3.1.0
news.caption: The app is now called SEUsign. Same seal mark on the icon, same on-device signer underneath.
